questions.question:
Which of the following is/are NOT true about the distance-time graph for a body moving in uniform motion?

(i) The slope of the distance-time graph gives the acceleration of the body.

(ii) The lesser the slope of the graph the slower the body is moving.

(iii) The area under this graph gives the speed of the body.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (i) and (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **distance-time graph**, the **slope** (gradient) is defined as the change in distance divided by the change in time (Δd/Δt), which represents the **speed** of the object. **Acceleration** is the rate of change of **velocity** over time and is not directly represented by the slope of a distance-time graph. ***Hence, statement (i) is incorrect.***
 
• For a body in **uniform motion**, the graph is a **straight line**. A **lesser slope** (a flatter line) indicates that the body covers less distance in a given time interval, meaning the magnitude of its **speed** is lower. ***Hence, statement (ii) is correct.***
 
• The **area under a graph** is the integral of the y-axis variable with respect to the x-axis variable. For a distance-time graph, this would be the product of **distance and time** (unit: meter·seconds), which does not correspond to **speed** (unit: meters per second) or any standard kinematic quantity. ***Hence, statement (iii) is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uniform Motion Characteristics**:

 
 
• An object is in **uniform motion** if it travels in a **straight line** and covers **equal distances** in **equal intervals of time**.
 
• In this state, the **velocity** is constant, and the resultant **acceleration** is zero.
 
• The **distance-time graph** is always a linear plot with a **constant gradient**.
 
 
 
• **Speed-Time (or Velocity-Time) Graphs**:
 
 
• In a **velocity-time graph**, the **slope** represent the **acceleration** of the body.
 
• The **area** under the velocity-time graph represents the **displacement** or total distance traveled by the body.
 
• For **uniform motion**, the velocity-time graph is a **horizontal line** parallel to the time axis, indicating a slope of zero (zero acceleration).

questions.question: A car of mass 1000 kg moving with a velocity of 20 m/s comes to rest in 10 s after applying the brakes. What is the value of the force applied by the brakes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**− 2000 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Newton's Second Law of Motion**, the force (F) applied to an object is directly proportional to the rate of change of its **linear momentum**, commonly expressed as **F = m × a**, where 'm' is mass and 'a' is acceleration.
 
• The **acceleration (a)** of the car is calculated using the first equation of motion or the definition of acceleration: **a = (v − u) / t**. Here, **u** is the initial velocity, **v** is the final velocity, and **t** is the time interval.
 
• Given parameters: **Mass (m) = 1000 kg**, **Initial Velocity (u) = 20 m/s**, **Final Velocity (v) = 0 m/s** (as the car comes to rest), and **Time (t) = 10 s**.
 
• Calculating acceleration: a = (0 − 20) / 10 = **−2 m/s²**. The negative sign indicates **retardation** or deceleration due to braking.
 
• Applying the force formula: F = 1000 kg × (−2 m/s²) = **−2000 N**. The negative sign signifies that the **braking force** is acting in the direction opposite to the car's motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kinematics and Dynamics:**

 
 
• **Newton (N):** The **SI unit of force**. One Newton is the force required to accelerate a mass of **1 kg** at a rate of **1 m/s²**.
 
• **Retardation:** It is defined as **negative acceleration**. In this case, the brakes provide a resistive force that reduces the **kinetic energy** of the vehicle.
 
• **Impulse:** The change in momentum (m × Δv) is also known as **impulse**, which is equal to the product of force and the time interval (F × t).
 
• **Direction of Force:** In physics, the sign of the force indicates **vector direction** relative to the chosen coordinate system; a negative result confirms it is a **resistive force**.

questions.question: The extent of bending of light rays achieved by a lens is expressed in terms of its ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Power**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Power of a lens** represents its capacity to bend light rays. It is defined as the **tangent of the angle** by which it converges or diverges a beam of light falling at a unit distant from the **optical center**.
 
• It is mathematically defined as the **reciprocal of the focal length** (f) of the lens. The formula is expressed as **P = 1/f**, where the focal length must be in **meters**.
 
• The **SI unit** of optical power is the **Dioptre** (represented by **D**). One Dioptre is equal to 1 m−¹.
 
• A **convex lens** has a positive focal length, and therefore its **power is positive**. Conversely, a **concave lens** has a negative focal length, making its **power negative**.
 
• A lens with a **shorter focal length** has a greater ability to bend light rays, meaning it has **higher power** compared to a lens with a longer focal length.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnification**:

 
 
• It is the **ratio** of the height of the image to the height of the object.
 
• It indicates how many times the image is **enlarged** or **diminished** relative to the object size.
 
 
 
• **Aperture**:
 
 
• It refers to the **effective diameter** of the light-transmitting area of the lens.
 
• The **intensity of the image** formed depends on the size of the aperture, as it controls the **amount of light** entering the system.
 
 
 
• **Image Distance**:
 
 
• It is the distance between the **optical center** of the lens and the **position of the image** formed, denoted by **v**.
 
• According to the **Lens Formula**, 1/f = 1/v − 1/u, where u is the object distance.

questions.question: What unique feature allows mitochondria to produce some of their own proteins?

options.text: They contain their own DNA and ribosomes.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They contain their own DNA and ribosomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mitochondria are often referred to as the **powerhouse of the cell** because they are the primary sites for **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)** synthesis through **aerobic respiration**.
 
• They are classified as **semi-autonomous organelles** because they possess their own genetic material, known as **mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA)**, and their own **ribosomes**.
 
• The **mtDNA** is typically a small, circular molecule that encodes for several essential **proteins**, **tRNAs**, and **rRNAs** required for the organelle's function.
 
• Mitochondria contain **70S ribosomes**, which are structurally similar to those found in **prokaryotic organisms**, allowing them to perform **protein synthesis** within the mitochondrial matrix independently of the cell nucleus.
 
• While most cellular proteins are encoded by **nuclear DNA** and imported from the **cytoplasm**, these organelles produce about 13 critical polypeptides involved in the **oxidative phosphorylation** system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Endosymbiotic Theory**:

 
 
• The presence of independent **DNA** and **ribosomes** supports the theory that mitochondria evolved from an ancient **endosymbiosis** between a **primitive eukaryote** and an **aerobic bacterium**.
 
 
 
• **Structural Components**:
 
 
• **Double Membrane**: Mitochondria consist of an **inner membrane** and an **outer membrane**. The inner membrane is folded into **cristae** to maximize the surface area for **energy production**.
 
• **Porous Outer Membrane**: This membrane contains special proteins called **porins**, which permit the free diffusion of molecules smaller than 5,000 Daltons.
 
 
 
• **ATP Production**:
 
 
• While mitochondria produce **ATP**, this is a metabolic function and does not directly provide the genetic blueprint or machinery for **protein manufacturing**.

questions.question:
1. A precipitation reaction occurs when two aqueous solutions react to form an insoluble solid.

2. The solid formed is called a precipitate.

3. All precipitation reactions involve acids and bases only.

Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 and 2 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **precipitation reaction** occurs when two **aqueous solutions** containing **soluble salts** are mixed together, resulting in a **double displacement reaction** that yields an **insoluble ionic solid**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **insoluble solid** that emerges from the liquid mixture is scientifically referred to as a **precipitate**, and its formation indicates that the product has exceeded its **solubility limit** in the given **solvent**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• While some **acid-base reactions** might produce a precipitate, the vast majority of precipitation reactions involve **salts**; conversely, acid-base reactions are fundamentally **neutralization reactions** that primarily produce **water** and a **soluble salt**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common Precipitation Examples:**

 
 
• **Silver Chloride (AgCl):** When **Silver Nitrate (AgNO₃)** reacts with **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, a **white precipitate** of **AgCl** is formed.
 
• **Barium Sulphate (BaSO₄):** The reaction between **Barium Chloride (BaCl₂)** and **Sodium Sulphate (Na₂SO₄)** produces a **white insoluble solid**.
 
• **Lead Iodide (PbI₂):** Mixing **Lead Nitrate** and **Potassium Iodide** results in a striking **yellow precipitate**.
 
 
 
• **Industrial and Laboratory Uses:**
 
 
• **Qualitative Analysis:** Used to detect the presence of specific **cations** or **anions** in an unknown solution based on the color and solubility of the precipitate.
 
• **Water Treatment:** Used to remove **contaminants** like **magnesium**, **calcium**, and **heavy metals** from **hard water** or industrial wastewater.
 
• **Pigment Production:** Many **industrial dyes** and **pigments** are manufactured through controlled precipitation processes.

questions.question: Which of the following salts, when dissolved in water, will produce a neutral solution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium chloride (NaCl)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sodium chloride (NaCl)** is classified as a **neutral salt** because it is the product of a neutralization reaction between a **strong acid** (Hydrochloric acid, HCl) and a **strong base** (Sodium hydroxide, NaOH).
 
• When dissolved in water, NaCl dissociates completely into its constituent ions, **Na⁺** and **Cl−**. These ions are the conjugate species of a strong base and a strong acid, respectively, and therefore have negligible tendency to react with water.
 
• Since neither the cation nor the anion undergoes **salt hydrolysis**, the concentration of **hydrogen ions (H⁺)** and **hydroxyl ions (OH−)** remains equal to that of pure water.
 
• Consequently, the **pH value** of the resulting aqueous solution is approximately **7.0** at 25°C, characterizing the solution as **neutral**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Potassium hydroxide (KOH)**:

 
 
• It is not a salt but a **strong base**. It dissociates to release a high concentration of **OH− ions**, resulting in a **strongly alkaline** solution with a pH typically greater than 13.
 
 
 
• **Ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl)**:
 
 
• This is an **acidic salt** formed from a **strong acid** (HCl) and a **weak base** (Ammonium hydroxide). The NH₄⁺ ion undergoes **cationic hydrolysis**, releasing H⁺ ions into the solution and lowering the pH below 7.
 
 
 
• **Sodium acetate (CH₃COONa)**:
 
 
• This is a **basic salt** derived from a **weak acid** (Acetic acid) and a **strong base** (NaOH). The acetate ion (CH₃COO−) undergoes **anionic hydrolysis**, producing OH− ions and making the solution **alkaline** (pH > 7).

questions.question: A gardener buried five different substances in a garden: banana peels, newspaper, cotton cloth, plastic bottle and metal spoon. How many of the substances he buried were biodegradable?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Among the five substances buried by the gardener, **Banana peels**, **Newspaper**, and **Cotton cloth** are the three that are classified as **biodegradable**.
 
• **Banana peels** are organic waste products from plants that consist of biological tissue, which **microorganisms** like bacteria and fungi can decompose into humus within approximately 2 to 5 weeks.
 
• **Newspaper** is primarily made from **wood pulp**, which contains **cellulose**; this organic compound is easily broken down by soil enzymes and moisture, typically taking 10 to 30 days to disappear.
 
• **Cotton cloth** is a natural textile derived from the **Gossypium** plant; because it is composed of natural fibers, it is susceptible to biological decay and generally decomposes within 2 to 5 months in a garden environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biodegradable** substances are materials that can be broken down into simpler, non-toxic substances by the action of living organisms like **decomposers**.

 
 
• Natural materials like **paper**, **wood**, **animal waste**, and **plant remains** are essential for maintaining the **nutrient cycle** in the soil.
 
• The process of biodegradation requires specific environmental conditions including **moisture**, **oxygen**, and the presence of **aerobic** or **anaerobic bacteria**.
 
 
 
• **Non-biodegradable** substances are materials that cannot be decomposed by biological processes and persist in the environment for long periods.
 
 
• **Plastic bottles** are made from synthetic polymers like **Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET)**, which lack the chemical bonds that bacteria can recognize and break, lasting for up to 450 years.
 
• **Metal spoons**, often made of **stainless steel** or **aluminum**, are inorganic and do not undergo biological decay, though they may eventually undergo **corrosion** or **oxidation** over centuries.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the arrangement of electrons in Thomson's atomic model?

options.text: Electrons are located at the center of the atom
Electrons are embedded in a positively charged sphere
Electrons are found only on the surface of the atom

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electrons are embedded in a positively charged sphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **J.J. Thomson** proposed his model of the atom in **1898**, shortly after he discovered the **electron**, the first subatomic particle.
 
• According to this model, an **atom** is envisioned as a **positively charged sphere** where **negatively charged electrons** are embedded into it, similar to seeds in a fruit.
 
• This model is widely known as the **Plum Pudding Model** or the **Watermelon Model** due to the specific arrangement of its components.
 
• In the **Watermelon** analogy, the red edible part represents the **positive charge** distributed throughout the atom, while the black seeds represent the **electrons**.
 
• Thomson hypothesized that the **magnitude** of the positive and negative charges is equal, which ensures that the atom remains **electrically neutral**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rutherford Atomic Model**:

 
 
• Unlike Thomson's static model, **Ernest Rutherford** proposed in **1911** that electrons **revolve around a nucleus** in circular paths.
 
• This model was based on the **Alpha-particle scattering experiment**, which proved the existence of a dense, central **nucleus**.
 
 
 
• **Bohr Atomic Model**:
 
 
• Proposed by **Niels Bohr** in **1913**, it refined the arrangement by stating that electrons move in **discrete orbits** with fixed energy levels.
 
 
 
• **Shortcomings of Thomson Model**:
 
 
• It could not explain the **stability of the atom** or the results of later experiments showing that most of an atom is **empty space**.
 
• It failed to account for the **scattering of alpha particles** through large angles, which necessitated the concept of a central **positive core**.

questions.question: The principal function of the plasma membrane is to:

options.text: Serve as the site of ATP synthesis.
Provide rigid support and prevent cell swelling.
Regulate movement of substances across the cell.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regulate movement of substances across the cell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **plasma membrane**, also referred to as the **cell membrane**, is a biological membrane that separates the interior of all cells from the outside environment.
 
• It is **selectively permeable**, which is its most vital characteristic, allowing it to control the **influx and efflux** of nutrients, ions, and metabolic waste products.
 
• The structure is primarily composed of a **phospholipid bilayer** with embedded **integral proteins** and **peripheral proteins** that act as channels or pumps.
 
• It maintains **homeostasis** within the cell by facilitating transport mechanisms such as **simple diffusion**, **facilitated diffusion**, and **active transport** using **ATP**.
 
• The **Fluid Mosaic Model** describes the membrane as a dynamic structure where proteins float in or on the fluid lipid bilayer, enabling **cell signaling** and **recognition**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ATP Synthesis**:

 
 
• In eukaryotic cells, the primary site for **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)** production is the **mitochondria** via the process of **oxidative phosphorylation**.
 
 
 
• **Cell Wall**:
 
 
• Provides **rigid support** and structural integrity; it is found in **plants (cellulose)**, **fungi (chitin)**, and **prokaryotes (peptidoglycan)** but is absent in animal cells.
 
 
 
• **Nucleus**:
 
 
• Acts as the **genetic control center** of the cell, housing the **chromosomes** and **DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid)**, protecting them from the metabolic activities of the cytoplasm.

questions.question: All of the following functions are performed by different components of a Xylem tissue, EXCEPT:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Transporting food from leaves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem** is a complex conducting tissue in vascular plants that primarily facilitates the **upward movement** of water and dissolved minerals from the roots.
 
• It consists of four specialized components: **tracheids**, **vessel elements**, **xylem parenchyma**, and **xylem fibers**.
 
• **Tracheids** and **vessels** are the primary water-conducting elements that form long, hollow tubes to ensure **vertical transport** of fluids throughout the plant.
 
• **Xylem fibers** are highly lignified, dead cells with thick walls that function to **provide mechanical support** and structural rigidity to the plant body.
 
• **Xylem parenchyma** is the only living component of the xylem tissue, specifically designed for **storing food** materials such as starch and assisting in lateral water conduction.
 
• The process of **transporting organic solutes** and food from the leaves to other parts of the plant is called **translocation**, which is the exclusive function of the **phloem** tissue.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phloem Tissue**:

 
 
• **Sieve Tube Elements**: These are long, tube-like structures that lack a nucleus at maturity and are responsible for the **bidirectional transport** of sucrose.
 
• **Companion Cells**: These specialized cells are closely associated with sieve tubes and maintain the **pressure gradient** required for nutrient movement.
 
• **Phloem Parenchyma**: Responsible for storing food and **secretion** of substances like resins and mucilage.
 
• **Direction of Flow**: While xylem flow is **unidirectional** (root to leaf), phloem flow is **multidirectional**, moving nutrients from source to sink.
 
 
 
• **Vascular Bundle**:
 
 
• The combination of **xylem** and **phloem** constitutes the vascular bundle, which serves as the **circulatory system** for higher plants.
 
• The **cambium** layer, found in dicotyledonous plants between xylem and phloem, is responsible for **secondary growth** and thickening of the stem.

questions.question: In the substitution reaction of methane (CH₄) with chlorine (Cl₂) under UV light, what is the first product formed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Methyl chloride (CH₃Cl).**__

• **The first substitution product of methane and chlorine is methyl chloride (CH₃Cl).**

• One hydrogen atom of methane is replaced by one chlorine atom during the first substitution step.

 __
 
• A reaction in which one atom or group in a molecule is replaced by another atom or group.
 
• Alkanes typically undergo free-radical substitution reactions with halogens.

• Formed during further chlorination of methyl chloride.
 
• Commonly used as an industrial solvent.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Tetrachloride (CCl₄)**__

• The final product when all four hydrogen atoms of methane are replaced by chlorine atoms.
 
• Historically used in fire extinguishers and cleaning agents.

questions.question:
When white light is incident obliquely on a glass prism, which of the following statement(s) is/are NOT true?

(i) Red colour undergoes minimum deviation.

(ii) The speed of violet colour is the least while travelling through the prism.

(iii) Refractive index of green colour is more than the violet colour.

(iv) Refractive index of red colour is more than blue colour.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (iii) and (iv)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When white light is incident on a **glass prism**, it undergoes **dispersion**, splitting into its constituent colors (VIBGYOR) because each color travels at a different speed in the glass medium.
 
• Statement (i) explains that **red light** has the **longest wavelength** in the visible spectrum; since the **angle of deviation** is inversely proportional to wavelength, red bends the least. ***Hence, statement (i) is correct.***
 
• Statement (ii) pertains to the speed of light, which is calculated as v = (c)/(n) . Because **violet light** experiences the highest **refractive index**, it travels at the slowest speed within the prism. ***Hence, statement (ii) is correct.***
 
• Statement (iii) suggests that green has a higher refractive index than violet. In reality, according to **Cauchy's formula**, the refractive index decreases as wavelength increases; since **violet** has a shorter wavelength than **green**, violet has a higher refractive index. ***Hence, statement (iii) is incorrect.***
 
• Statement (iv) claims the refractive index of red is more than blue. However, **red light** has a significantly longer wavelength than **blue light**, resulting in a lower refractive index for red. ***Hence, statement (iv) is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refractive Index and Wavelength Relationship**:

 
 
• The **refractive index (n)** of a material is not constant but varies with the frequency of light, a phenomenon known as **chromatic dispersion**.
 
• **Violet Light**: It has the shortest wavelength (approximately **400 nm**) and highest frequency, leading to the **maximum deviation** from the original path.
 
• **Red Light**: It has the longest wavelength (approximately **700 nm**) and lowest frequency, leading to the **minimum deviation**.
 
• **Visible Spectrum Order**: The sequence from longest to shortest wavelength is **Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, and Violet**.

questions.question: A cyclist riding at constant speed on a circular track is an example of which type of motion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uniform circular motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uniform circular motion** is defined as the motion of an object traveling at a **constant speed** along a **circular path**.
 
• In this scenario, while the **cyclist** maintains a steady speed, the **direction of motion** changes continuously at every point along the circular track, meaning the **velocity** is constantly changing.
 
• Because the velocity is changing due to the direction, the cyclist undergoes **centripetal acceleration**, which is always directed toward the **center of the circle**.
 
• The **magnitude of velocity** (speed) remains unchanged, which distinguishes it from non-uniform circular motion where the speed would fluctuate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Linear Motion**:

 
 
• Also referred to as **rectilinear motion**, it occurs when an object moves in a **straight line**.
 
• In this type of motion, the **direction** remains constant unless the object reverses its path.
 
 
 
• **Oscillatory Motion**:
 
 
• This is the **to-and-fro** or **periodic motion** of an object about a **fixed mean position**.
 
• Classic examples include the movement of a **simple pendulum** or a **tuning fork**.
 
 
 
• **Non-uniform Motion**:
 
 
• An object is said to be in **non-uniform motion** if its **speed** changes as it moves, covering unequal distances in equal intervals of time.
 
• If the cyclist were **accelerating** or **braking** on the track, the motion would be classified as non-uniform circular motion.

questions.question: In a homogeneous mixture, the size of particles of solute is typically:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Less than 1 nm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **homogeneous mixture** is a type of mixture where the components are distributed with uniform composition and properties throughout the entire mass, commonly known as a **True Solution**.
 
• In a **True Solution**, the size of the **solute particles** is extremely small, typically measuring **less than 1 nanometer** (1 nm = 10−⁹ meters) in diameter.
 
• Because these particles are at the **molecular or ionic level**, they cannot be seen even with the aid of a powerful **microscope**.
 
• Due to their minute size, they do not scatter a beam of light passing through the medium, meaning they do not exhibit the **Tyndall effect**.
 
• These particles pass easily through **filter paper** and **parchment membranes**, making them impossible to separate from the **solvent** using standard filtration techniques.
 
• The mixture is highly **stable**, and the solute particles do not settle down when left undisturbed because of their constant **kinetic motion** and negligible mass.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Colloids**:

 
 
• These are **heterogeneous mixtures** where the particle size ranges between **1 nm and 1000 nm**.
 
• They are large enough to scatter a beam of light (**Tyndall effect**) but small enough to remain suspended indefinitely without settling.
 
 
 
• **Suspensions**:
 
 
• These are **heterogeneous mixtures** containing large particles, typically **larger than 1000 nm** (1 μm).
 
• The particles are **visible to the naked eye**, do not pass through filter paper, and eventually settle at the bottom due to **gravity**.
 
 
 
• **Units of Measurement**:
 
 
• **1 Nanometer (nm)** is equal to 10−⁹ meters.
 
• **1 Micrometer (μm)** is equal to 10−⁶ meters or 1000 nm.

__
 
• The **neuron** or nerve cell is the structural and functional unit of the **nervous system**, specialized for the reception and transmission of electrical impulses.
 
• A typical neuron consists of three distinct regions: the **cell body (Cyton)**, **dendrites**, and a single **axon**.
 
• The **axon** is a long, slender, and single cytoplasmic extension that originates from the **axon hillock**; its primary role is to carry **nerve impulses** away from the cell body toward a **synapse** or effector organ.
 
• **Dendrites** are the multiple, short, and highly **branched protoplasmic processes** that project from the cell body.
 
• The primary function of dendrites is to receive **afferent signals** (stimuli) from other neurons or sensory receptors and conduct them toward the **soma** or cell body.

• **Protective connective tissue**:
 
 
• In the peripheral nervous system, nerves are bundled and protected by layers such as the **epineurium**, **perineurium**, and **endoneurium**.
 
• The **myelin sheath**, produced by **Schwann cells**, provides electrical insulation around the axon.
 
 
 
• **Rapid stimulus transmission**:
 
 
• This refers to the functional efficiency of the axon, especially those that are **myelinated**.

questions.question: Which of the following is represented by a circle with the letter 'V' in a circuit diagram?

• In electrical circuit diagrams, a **voltmeter** is represented by a **circle** with the uppercase letter **'V'** inscribed inside it.
 
• The primary function of this instrument is to measure the **potential difference** (voltage) between two specific points in an electric circuit, with the standard unit being the **Volt (V)**.
 
• To ensure measurement accuracy, a voltmeter is always connected in **parallel** with the component whose voltage is being measured, as voltage remains constant across parallel branches.
 
• A characteristic feature of a voltmeter is its **high internal resistance**; this prevents it from drawing significant current from the main circuit. In theoretical physics, an **ideal voltmeter** is considered to have **infinite resistance**.
 
• The sensitivity of the device can be modified using a high-value resistor, known as a **multiplier**, connected in series with the internal galvanometer mechanism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is used to vary the **current** in a circuit by manually changing the **resistance** value without interrupting the circuit flow.
 
 
 
• **Vacuum Diode**:
 
 
• A legacy electronic device symbolized by a circle containing a **cathode** and an **anode**.
 
• It functions as a **rectifier**, allowing electric current to flow in only one direction, and was the precursor to the modern semiconductor **p-n junction diode**.

• Often represented by a functional block or a **Zener diode** symbol (a triangle with a 'Z' shaped bar).

questions.question: Which of the following is true about Fleming’s left-hand rule?

options.text: If the thumb points in the direction of force and the forefinger in the direction of current, the middle finger shows the direction of magnetic field.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**If the forefinger points in the direction of magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of current, the thumb shows the direction of motion or force on the conductor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fleming’s Left-Hand Rule** is a mnemonic used to determine the direction of force acting on a **current-carrying conductor** when placed within an external **magnetic field**. **Hence, statement 2 is correct.**
 
• The rule assigns the **Thumb** to the direction of **Force** (or motion), the **Forefinger** to the **Magnetic Field**, and the **Middle Finger** to the **Electric Current**, provided they are held mutually perpendicular. **Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.**
 
• This principle is the fundamental basis for the operation of **Electric Motors**, where electrical energy is converted into mechanical motion, and **Loudspeakers**. **Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.**
 
• Correct orientation requires the **Forefinger** to represent the field and the **Middle Finger** to represent the current to correctly identify the **Thumb** as the force vector. **Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Physical Components**:

 
 
• **Magnetic Field (B)**: Represents the flux lines moving from the **North Pole** to the **South Pole**.
 
• **Electric Current (I)**: Represents the flow of conventional current (from positive to negative).
 
• **Force (F)**: Also known as the **Lorentz Force**, it is calculated by the formula **F = BIL sin(θ)**, where θ is the angle between the conductor and the field.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Right-Hand Rule**:
 
 
• While the **Left-Hand Rule** is applied to **Motors** (input current produces motion), **Fleming’s Right-Hand Rule** is applied to **Generators** (input motion produces induced current).
 
• In the right-hand version, the **Thumb** represents motion, the **Forefinger** field, and the **Middle Finger** represents the direction of the **Induced Current**.
 
 
 
• **Applications**:
 
 
• Used in designing **Galvanometers**, **DC Motors**, and electromagnetic actuators.
 
• Critical for understanding how **charged particles** (like electrons or protons) deflect when entering a magnetic field in **Particle Accelerators**.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the size of an atom.

Statement 1: The size of an atom is approximately in the range of 0.1 nm to 0.5 nm.

Statement 2: Atomic size increases as we move from left to right in a period of the periodic table.

Statement 3: The radius of a hydrogen atom is about 10⁻¹⁰ meters.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **atomic size** refers to the distance between the center of the **nucleus** and the outermost shell of an atom. Most atoms have a size or diameter that falls within the range of **0.1 nm to 0.5 nm** (1 to 5 Angstroms). **Hence, statement 1 is correct.**
 
• Across a **period** in the **modern periodic table**, the **atomic radius** actually **decreases** from left to right. This occurs because the **atomic number** increases, leading to a higher **nuclear charge** (more protons) that pulls the **valence electrons** closer to the nucleus, despite them being in the same energy level. **Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.**
 
• The **hydrogen atom** is the smallest neutral atom. Its **atomic radius** is approximately **37 pm** (picometers) to **53 pm** (Bohr radius). In terms of order of magnitude, 1 Angstrom is equal to **10−¹⁰ m**, which represents the standard scale for the radius of a hydrogen atom. **Hence, statement 3 is correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Group Trends**:

 
 
• In a **group**, the atomic size **increases** from top to bottom.
 
• This is due to the addition of **new electron shells** at each successive element, which increases the distance between the **nucleus** and the outermost electrons, overriding the increase in **nuclear charge**.
 
 
 
• **Measurement Units**:
 
 
• **Nanometer (nm)**: 1 nm = **10−⁹ m**.
 
• **Angstrom (Å)**: 1 Å = **10−¹⁰ m** or **0.1 nm**.
 
• **Picometer (pm)**: 1 pm = **10−¹² m**.
 
 
 
• **Effective Nuclear Charge (Zₑff)**:
 
 
• This is the net positive charge experienced by an electron in a **multi-electron atom**. It is the primary driver for the contraction of **atomic size** across a **period**.

questions.question: Newton’s first law of motion explains the concept of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Balanced forces**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton’s First Law of Motion**, often referred to as the **Law of Inertia**, states that an object will persist in its state of **rest** or **uniform motion** in a straight line unless acted upon by an external **unbalanced force**.
 
• The law fundamentally explains the behavior of objects under the influence of **balanced forces**, which occurs when the **vector sum** of all external forces acting on a body is exactly **zero**.
 
• When forces are **balanced**, there is no change in the **magnitude** or **direction** of the object’s velocity, meaning the **acceleration** remains zero.
 
• This principle was first published by **Sir Isaac Newton** in **1687** within his monumental work, **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica**, establishing the foundation for **Classical Mechanics**.
 
• The law serves as a qualitative definition of **force** as the external agent capable of changing a body's **state of inertia**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inertia**:

 
 
• It is the **inherent property** of matter that resists changes in its state of motion or rest.
 
• The **mass** of an object is the quantitative measure of its **inertia**; objects with higher mass require greater force to change their velocity.
 
• Common examples include **Inertia of Rest** (dust falling from a carpet when beaten) and **Inertia of Motion** (passengers falling forward when a moving bus brakes suddenly).
 
 
 
• **Net Force and Acceleration**:
 
 
• A **non-zero net force** refers to **unbalanced forces**, which cause an object to **accelerate** as per **Newton’s Second Law**.
 
• **Continuous acceleration** implies a constant application of an **unbalanced force**, which contradicts the equilibrium state described in the First Law.
 
• The **change in momentum** is defined as the product of mass and the change in velocity, which is directly proportional to the **impressed force**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an application of the Archimede's Principle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Speedometers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Archimedes' Principle** states that when a body is immersed fully or partially in a fluid, it experiences an upward **buoyant force** that is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it.
 
• **Speedometers** are instruments designed to measure and display the instantaneous speed of a vehicle. They typically function using **Eddy currents**, **magnetic sensors**, or **GPS technology** and do not rely on fluid displacement or buoyancy.
 
• **Lactometers** are used to determine the purity of milk by measuring its **density**. Since the instrument floats at different levels based on the fluid's weight and displacement, it is a direct application of **Archimedes' Principle**.
 
• **Hydrometers** are devices used to measure the **specific gravity** or **relative density** of liquids. They operate by observing the depth to which a calibrated glass tube sinks in a liquid, which is governed by the **upward thrust** of the displaced fluid.
 
• The **Designing of submarines** and ships heavily relies on this principle to ensure stability and **buoyancy**. Submarines specifically utilize **ballast tanks** to alter their weight by taking in or discharging water, allowing them to submerge or surface by manipulating the **displaced volume**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buoyant Force**:

 
 
• It is the **upward force** exerted by a fluid on an object.
 
• The magnitude of this force is calculated as the product of the **density of the fluid**, the **acceleration due to gravity**, and the **volume of the displaced fluid**.
 
 
 
• **Specific Gravity**:
 
 
• It is a dimensionless quantity representing the ratio of the density of a substance to the density of **pure water** at 4 degrees Celsius.
 
• Instruments like **Hydrometers** use this ratio to identify the composition of various liquids like battery acid or antifreeze.
 
 
 
• **Eddy Current Mechanism**:
 
 
• Found in traditional **speedometers**, where a rotating magnet creates a **magnetic field** that induces currents in a non-ferrous metal cup, creating torque without physical contact.

questions.question: The primary purpose of check-dams in irrigation is to ______________.

options.text: To worsen erosion of top soil
To increase groundwater by storing rainwater
To channel river water for factory operations
To lower the quality of the soil

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To increase groundwater by storing rainwater**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **check-dam** is a small, often temporary, barrier constructed across a drainage ditch, swale, or channel to lower the **velocity of flow**.
 
• The primary objective of these structures is to promote **groundwater recharge**. By slowing down the surface runoff, the dam creates a small pool that allows water to **percolate** through the soil layers into the **underground aquifers**.
 
• In **arid and semi-arid regions**, check-dams serve as a vital tool for **water harvesting**, ensuring that rainwater is not lost as flash floods but is instead stored beneath the surface for future **irrigation** needs.
 
• These structures significantly reduce **soil erosion** by trapping **sediments** and silt, which would otherwise be carried away by fast-moving water, thus preserving the **fertility** of the land.
 
• By maintaining a higher **water table**, check-dams ensure that nearby **borewells** and open wells remain functional even during the dry summer months.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Watershed Management**:

 
 
• Check-dams are a core component of **integrated watershed management**, which aims to conserve every drop of rain within a specific geographical area.
 
• They can be constructed using various materials such as **boulders**, **gabions** (wire cages filled with rocks), logs, or **reinforced concrete**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact**:
 
 
• Unlike large-scale dams, check-dams have a **minimal ecological footprint** and do not involve large-scale displacement of local populations.
 
• They improve **soil moisture** content, which directly benefits the growth of **natural vegetation** and crops in the immediate vicinity.
 
• **Siltation control** provided by these dams prevents the clogging of larger downstream reservoirs and riverbeds.

questions.question: If mass is doubled and g remains constant, weight becomes ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Double**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Weight** of an object is defined as the **gravitational force** with which a celestial body, such as the Earth, attracts the object toward its center.
 
• Mathematically, weight is expressed by the formula **W = m × g**, where **m** represents the **mass** of the object and **g** represents the **acceleration due to gravity**.
 
• This equation indicates that weight is **directly proportional** to the mass of the object when the gravitational acceleration remains constant.
 
• If the **mass** is doubled (2m) and **g** is kept constant, the new weight (Wₙₑw) becomes **(2m) × g**, which is equivalent to **2W**.
 
• Consequently, any linear change in mass results in an identical linear change in weight, provided the **gravitational field strength** does not fluctuate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mass:**

 
 
• It is a **scalar quantity** that measures the **inertia** or the total **quantity of matter** within a body.
 
• The **SI unit** of mass is the **kilogram (kg)**, and it remains **constant** regardless of the object's location in the universe.
 
 
 
• **Weight:**
 
 
• It is a **vector quantity** because it has a specific direction, which is always towards the **center of the planet**.
 
• The **SI unit** of weight is the **Newton (N)**.
 
• Unlike mass, weight varies depending on the value of **g**; for instance, an object's weight on the **Moon** is approximately **1/6th** of its weight on Earth due to the Moon's weaker gravity.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g):**
 
 
• On the surface of the Earth, its standard value is taken as **9.8 m/s²**.
 
• It reaches its **maximum** at the **poles** and its **minimum** at the **equator**, and becomes zero at the **center of the Earth**.

__
 
• **SONAR** is an acronym for **Sound Navigation and Ranging**. It is a sophisticated device that utilizes **ultrasonic waves** to determine the **distance**, **direction**, and **speed** of underwater objects such as **submarines**, **icebergs**, or **sunken ships**.
 
• The system typically comprises a **transmitter** and a **detector** mounted on the hull of a vessel. The **transmitter** emits high-frequency **ultrasound waves** that travel through the water medium.
 
• When these waves encounter an object or the **seabed**, they are reflected back as **echoes**. These reflected waves are captured by the **detector**, which converts the acoustic energy into **electrical signals** for processing.
 
• The distance to the object is calculated using the formula 2d = v × t, where 'd' is the distance, 'v' is the **speed of sound** in water, and 't' is the total **time interval** between the transmission and reception. This specific technique is known as **echo-ranging**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ultrasound** refers to sound waves with frequencies above **20,000 Hz**, which are beyond the **audible range** of human hearing.
 
• Different scientific instruments serve the other functions mentioned:
 
 
• **Barometer**: A scientific instrument primarily used to measure **atmospheric pressure** to forecast weather changes.
 
• **Ammeter**: An electrical instrument used to measure the **electric current** flowing through a circuit in **Amperes**.
 
• **Pyrometer**: A type of remote-sensing thermometer used to measure exceptionally **high temperatures** of surfaces, often in industrial furnaces.
 
 
 
• **SONAR** is also used by marine animals like **bats** and **dolphins** (biological sonar) for **echolocation** to navigate and find prey in dark or murky environments.

questions.question: A block of mass 20 kg is dropped from the top of a building of height 200 m. What will be the velocity with which the block will hit the ground? (Take the value of g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20√10 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The block is in a state of **free fall**, which occurs when an object is **dropped** from a height and moves solely under the influence of **gravity**.
 
• The **initial velocity (u)** is **0 m/s** because the object starts from a stationary position at the top of the **200 m** building.
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity (g)** is constant and given as **10 m/s²**, acting downwards towards the ground.
 
• To find the **final velocity (v)**, we utilize the **third equation of motion**: v² = u² + 2gh .
 
• By substituting the known values, the equation becomes: v² = 0² + 2 × 10 × 200 .
 
• Simplifying the expression leads to v² = 4000 .
 
• The **final velocity (v)** is obtained by taking the **square root** of the result: v = sqrt{4000} = sqrt{400 × 10} = 20sqrt{10} **m/s**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Equations of Motion**:

 
 
• These equations are valid only for objects moving with **uniform acceleration**.
 
• **First Equation**: v = u + at relates velocity and time.
 
• **Second Equation**: s = ut + (1)/(2)at² relates displacement and time.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Energy**:
 
 
• The **Potential Energy (PE)** at the top ( mgh ) is converted into **Kinetic Energy (KE)** at the ground ( (1)/(2)mv² ).
 
• Equating **PE** and **KE** shows that the **velocity** is **independent of mass**, as the variable **m** cancels out from both sides.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall Characteristics**:
 
 
• In a vacuum, a **20 kg** block and a lighter object would hit the ground with the **same velocity** if dropped from the same **height**.
 
• The **displacement (s)** in vertical motion is simply the **height (h)** of the fall.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly explains the working principle of dialysis in an artificial kidney?

options.text: Dialysis reabsorbs essential nutrients and salts like a normal kidney.
Dialysis removes wastes from blood by diffusion across a semi-permeable membrane.
Dialysis removes nitrogenous wastes from blood through active transport.
Dialysis uses high pressure to force wastes out of the blood into the dialysing fluid.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dialysis removes wastes from blood by diffusion across a semi-permeable membrane.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **artificial kidney** is a specialized medical device used to perform **hemodialysis**, which filters **nitrogenous waste products** from the blood in patients suffering from **renal failure**.
 
• The device contains a series of tubes with a **semi-permeable lining** (typically made of **cellulose**) that are submerged in a tank filled with **dialysing fluid**. Hence, the membrane serves as a selective barrier.
 
• The **dialysing fluid** is formulated to have an **osmotic pressure** identical to blood but is entirely devoid of nitrogenous wastes like **urea** and **uric acid**.
 
• Waste products move from the blood into the dialysing fluid by **diffusion**, a passive process driven by the concentration gradient across the membrane. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
 
• In a biological kidney, the **renal tubules** perform **selective reabsorption** of **glucose**, **amino acids**, and **salts**; however, an artificial kidney lacks this reabsorption capability. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.
 
• The movement of solutes in dialysis does not involve **active transport**, which requires **ATP** or cellular energy to move molecules against a gradient. Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.
 
• While the human **Glomerulus** utilizes high **hydrostatic pressure** for **ultrafiltration**, the fundamental working principle of the dialysis machine is chemical exchange via diffusion. Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nitrogenous Waste Products**:

 
 
• **Urea**: The primary waste product formed in the **liver** during the breakdown of proteins.
 
• **Creatinine**: A metabolic byproduct of **muscle metabolism** that must be cleared to prevent toxicity.
 
 
 
• **Dialysing Fluid Composition**:
 
 
• Contains **electrolytes** such as **Sodium**, **Potassium**, and **Calcium** at physiological levels.
 
• Includes **Bicarbonate** to help regulate the **pH level** of the patient’s blood and neutralize acidity.
 
• Maintains an **isotonic** state relative to healthy blood to prevent unwanted fluid shifts.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason for carbon’s versatility?

options.text: Ability to form single, double and triple bonds

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Formation of ionic bonds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Carbon is situated in **Group 14** of the periodic table with an **atomic number of 6** and an electronic configuration of 2, 4. This means it has four electrons in its outermost shell, leading to the property of **Tetravalency**.
 
• The term **Catenation** refers to carbon's unique ability to form strong **covalent bonds** with other carbon atoms. This allows for the creation of exceptionally long chains, branched structures, and complex rings, which is the foundation of **Organic Chemistry**.
 
• Due to its small atomic size, carbon can form multiple bonds, including **Single Bonds**, **Double Bonds**, and **Triple Bonds**. This is possible because the carbon nucleus can effectively hold the shared electrons in **pπ-pπ** orbital overlaps.
 
• Carbon does not form **Ionic Bonds** because losing four electrons to form a **C⁴⁺** ion requires an enormous amount of **Ionization Energy**. Conversely, gaining four electrons to form a **C⁴⁻** ion would be highly unstable, as a nucleus with six protons cannot easily hold ten electrons.
 
• The versatility of carbon is strictly due to its ability to **share electrons** and form stable covalent structures, rather than the transfer of electrons associated with ionic bonding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tetravalency**:

 
 
• Enables carbon to bond with four other atoms of carbon or atoms of other monovalent elements like **Hydrogen**, **Chlorine**, or **Bromine**.
 
• It allows for **directional bonding**, leading to various geometric shapes like **Tetrahedral**, **Trigonal Planar**, and **Linear**.
 
 
 
• **Catenation**:
 
 
• While elements like **Silicon** or **Sulfur** show catenation, the **C-C bond energy** is much higher, making carbon chains far more stable and less reactive to air and water.
 
• This property allows for the existence of **Isomers**, where compounds have the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements.
 
 
 
• **Multiple Bond Formation**:
 
 
• Carbon forms stable multiple bonds with **Oxygen**, **Nitrogen**, and **Sulfur**, which are essential for the functional groups found in biological molecules like proteins and DNA.
 
• The strength of these bonds is attributed to the **Small Atomic Radius** of carbon, which ensures a strong nuclear pull on the bonding pair of electrons.

questions.question: Where in the body would you expect to find a single layer of extremely thin, flat epithelial cells designed for the transport of substances (gases) across a delicate lining?

options.text: Skin, to prevent wear and tear
Lining of kidney tubules, for mechanical support
Lining of lung alveoli, for gas exchange
Inner lining of the intestine, for absorption

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lining of lung alveoli, for gas exchange**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The tissue described is the **Simple Squamous Epithelium**, which is characterized by a **single layer** of extremely thin, flat, and scale-like cells.
 
• These cells form a delicate lining that facilitates the **transport of substances** across a **semi-permeable membrane** through the process of **diffusion**.
 
• In the **Lung Alveoli**, this thinness is critical for the efficient exchange of **Oxygen** and **Carbon Dioxide** between the air sacs and the surrounding capillaries.
 
• Due to its minimal thickness, it provides the shortest possible distance for **gas molecules** to travel, ensuring rapid **respiratory exchange**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stratified Squamous Epithelium**:

 
 
• Found in the **Skin**, where epithelial cells are arranged in many layers to prevent **wear and tear** and provide protection to the body.
 
 
 
• **Cuboidal Epithelium**:
 
 
• Found in the **Lining of Kidney Tubules** and ducts of **salivary glands**.
 
• Consists of cube-shaped cells that provide **mechanical support** and assist in secretion and absorption.
 
 
 
• **Columnar Epithelium**:
 
 
• Found in the **Inner Lining of the Intestine**, where tall, pillar-like cells facilitate **absorption** and secretion.
 
• In parts like the respiratory tract, these may have **Cilia** (hair-like projections) to move mucus forward.

questions.question: In chemical industries, bleaching powder acts mainly as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**An oxidising agent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bleaching powder**, chemically identified as **Calcium Hypochlorite**, has the molecular formula **CaOCl₂**. It is widely recognized as a powerful **oxidising agent** in various industrial chemical processes.
 
• Its oxidative capability stems from its ability to release **nascent oxygen**. When bleaching powder reacts with **moisture** or **dilute acids**, it liberates **Chlorine gas**, which subsequently forms **Hypochlorous acid** (HClO) in the presence of water.
 
• The **Hypochlorous acid** further decomposes to yield **Nascent Oxygen** ([O]). This nascent oxygen is highly reactive and facilitates the **oxidation** of colored organic compounds, turning them into colorless substances, which is the fundamental mechanism of **bleaching**.
 
• In the **Textile Industry**, it is used for bleaching **cotton** and **linen**, while in the **Paper Industry**, it is utilized to whiten **wood pulp**.
 
• Beyond bleaching, its role as an **oxidising agent** makes it essential for **disinfecting drinking water** supplies by destroying bacteria and other harmful microorganisms through **cellular oxidation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chemical Preparation**:

 
 
• Bleaching powder is manufactured by the action of **Chlorine gas** on **dry slaked lime** (Calcium Hydroxide, **Ca(OH)₂**).
 
• The industrial production typically occurs in a **Hasenclever plant** or a **Bachmann plant**.
 
 
 
• **Conceptual Distinctions**:
 
 
• **Reducing Agent**: These substances donate electrons and undergo oxidation themselves. Bleaching powder acts as an **electron acceptor**, making it the opposite of a reducing agent.
 
• **Neutralising Agent**: These are used to balance **pH levels** in acid-base reactions. Although bleaching powder is slightly **basic**, its primary industrial utility is its **redox potential** rather than its acidity-correcting properties.
 
• **Catalyst**: A substance that speeds up a reaction without being consumed. Bleaching powder is a **reactant** that is chemically transformed during the bleaching and disinfection process.
 
• **Chloroform Production**: It is also used as a key reagent in the synthesis of **Chloroform** (CHCl₃) through its reaction with ethanol or acetone.

questions.question: A sound source has a frequency of 50 Hz. How many vibrations does it complete in one minute?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Frequency** is defined as the number of complete **cycles**, **vibrations**, or **oscillations** that occur per unit of time. The standard **SI unit** for frequency is the **Hertz (Hz)**.
 
• One **Hertz** corresponds to one **vibration per second**. Therefore, a sound source with a frequency of **50 Hz** completes exactly **50 vibrations** every second.
 
• The time duration provided in the problem is **one minute**. To calculate the total number of vibrations using the standard formula, the time must be converted into **seconds**.
 
• Since **1 minute** is equal to **60 seconds**, the total time interval for the observation is 60 seconds.
 
• The total number of vibrations is calculated by multiplying the **frequency** by the **total time** (Total Vibrations = Frequency × Time).
 
• Substituting the values: **50 vibrations/second × 60 seconds = 3000 vibrations**. Thus, the source completes 3000 full cycles in one minute.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Time Period (T):** It is the time required for one complete vibration. It is the **inverse of frequency** (T = 1/f). For a frequency of **50 Hz**, the time period is 1/50 = **0.02 seconds**.
 
• **Audible Range:** The range of frequencies that the average human ear can perceive is between **20 Hz and 20,000 Hz**. A 50 Hz sound is within the **audible spectrum** and is perceived as a very **low-pitched** sound.
 
• **Pitch and Frequency:** The **pitch** of a sound depends on the frequency of the vibration. **Higher frequency** results in a **high-pitched** or shrill sound, whereas **lower frequency** results in a **deep** or bass sound.
 
• **Infrasonic and Ultrasonic:**
 
 
• Frequencies below **20 Hz** are known as **infrasonic** sounds, which are often produced by **earthquakes** or large animals like **elephants**.
 
• Frequencies above **20,000 Hz** are known as **ultrasonic** sounds, used in **medical imaging (Ultrasound)** and by animals like **bats** for navigation.
 
 
 
• **Wave Equation:** The relationship between the speed of sound (v), frequency (f), and wavelength (λ) is given by **v = f × λ**.

questions.question: An electric oven has a power of 1200 W when it is operated at 100 V. How much will be the current flowing through the oven?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12 A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between **Electric Power**, **Voltage**, and **Current** is governed by the formula **P = V × I**, where **P** represents power in **Watts**, **V** represents potential difference in **Volts**, and **I** represents current in **Amperes**.
 
• According to the question, the **Power (P)** of the electric oven is **1200 W** and the **Voltage (V)** at which it is operated is **100 V**.
 
• To calculate the **Current (I)** flowing through the oven, the formula is rearranged as **I = P / V**.
 
• Substituting the given values into the equation: **I = 1200 / 100**.
 
• The calculation yields **I = 12 A**, indicating that a current of twelve amperes flows through the heating element of the oven when it is connected to the specified power source.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electric Power (P)**:

 
 
• The **SI unit** of power is the **Watt (W)**, named after **James Watt**.
 
• It describes the rate at which **Electrical Energy** is dissipated or consumed in an electric circuit.
 
• **1 Watt** is equivalent to **1 Joule per second**.
 
 
 
• **Electric Current (I)**:
 
 
• Measured in **Amperes (A)**, it is the rate of flow of **Electrons** or **Electric Charge** through a conductor.
 
• One Ampere is defined as the flow of one **Coulomb** of charge per second.
 
 
 
• **Relationship with Resistance**:
 
 
• Based on **Ohm's Law** (**V = IR**), power can also be expressed in terms of **Resistance (R)**.
 
• Alternative formulas include **P = I²R** and **P = V² / R**.
 
• In this specific case, the **Resistance** of the oven can be calculated as **R = V / I = 100 / 12 ≈ 8.33 Ω**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT known to reproduce through fission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hydra** is a multicellular freshwater organism belonging to the phylum **Cnidaria**. It is primarily known for reproducing through **budding**, an asexual process where a small outgrowth or bud forms on the parent body due to repeated **mitotic cell divisions** at a specific site.
 
• Once the bud matures and develops tiny tentacles and a mouth, it constricts at the base and detaches to become a new **independent organism**. This is distinct from **fission**, which involves the splitting of a single parent cell.
 
• **Amoeba**, **Leishmania**, and **Paramecium** are all **unicellular protozoans** that reproduce through various forms of **fission**, where the parent cell divides into two or more daughter cells.
 
• **Fission** is the simplest method of asexual reproduction in single-celled organisms, while **Hydra** utilizes more complex cellular differentiation and **regenerative cells** for its reproductive processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amoeba**:

 
 
• Reproduces via **simple binary fission**, where the division of the nucleus and cytoplasm can occur along any plane or axis.
 
 
 
• **Leishmania**:
 
 
• The causative parasite of **Kala-azar** (Visceral Leishmaniasis).
 
• It exhibits **binary fission** in a definite **longitudinal orientation** in relation to its whip-like **flagellum**.
 
 
 
• **Paramecium**:
 
 
• A ciliated protozoan that typically undergoes **transverse binary fission**.
 
• It possesses two types of nuclei, a **macronucleus** and a **micronucleus**, both of which participate in the division process to ensure genetic continuity.
